page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 6 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between raw compute and memory subsystem performance. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core CPU performance (787.9 in stress-ng, bottom 10%) and weak multi-core performance (4703.94 in stress-ng, bottom 25%). However, memory subsystem metrics are more resilient, with cached read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 616.67 GB/sec (average) and uncached large block read-only bandwidth at 43.56 GB/sec (average). Large block write bandwidth is weaker at 24.88 GB/sec. General utility benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (1351.0) and multi-core (5544.0), fall within the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of this server lies in its shared CPU model, which limits sustained high-compute tasks but offers a cost-efficient entry point for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. Static web serving throughput is relatively low at 5.86 GB/sec, and medium-model LLM prompt processing is weak at 21.93 tokens/sec. Conversely, the server performs adequately in software compilation (7888.0 on Geekbench clang) and database operations (3941.27 on PassMark). This profile is suitable for development environments, lightweight database operations, text processing, and general-purpose utility workloads.
